correctness.rationale: For any affine plane, the exact B B^T=q I+J and line intersection/parallel identities give the five explicit orthogonal adjacency spectral projectors and complete multiplicities. Restricting each projector to the sink pair yields principal ranks one, nonprincipal restricted Gram determinants positive for \(q\ge3\), and zero-mode ranks 0,1,2 as proved. The non-Hermitian dissipative bright/dark decomposition rigorously justifies eventual capture as the bright orthogonal projector, independent of strictly positive loss rates and nonzero hopping. The site law for incident point/line is verified by seven exact symbolic substitutions. Independent numerical full-adjacency eigendecomposition compared all site capture probabilities for 475 finite pairs (exhaustive 210 pairs at q=3) with maximum discrepancy \(5.33\times10^{-15}\); 56 incident-pair histograms and exact algebraic certificates passed. No finite test is used as the infinite-family proof.

value.rationale: Two-target placement is a natural control in coherent exciton/single-particle capture networks. The theorem gives a nontrivial exact optimality distinction among point, incident, parallel-line and intersecting-line sinks on every finite affine plane, including arbitrary coordinate-free examples: a geometrically parallel sink pair loses precisely one bright eigenmode relative to an intersecting pair. It further determines the entire local absorption histogram for an incident point-line pair, a physically relevant finite-design benchmark inaccessible from an average alone. The result is not an arbitrary small-size census or merely a restatement of the general Krylov formula.
